description: Security knowledge for SentinelAI. Evidence rules turn counted events into base facts; logic rules derive conclusions by forward chaining; classification maps conclusions to threat levels.

evidence_rules.description: 5+ failed logins against a device within 3 ticks
one source made 5+ failed logins against one target within 3 ticks
a successful login from source to target in the last 5 ticks
device ran a port scan in the last 5 ticks
unusual traffic from source to target in the last 3 ticks
unusual traffic on 2+ occasions within 3 ticks
unauthorized access attempt in the last 6 ticks

rules.name: R1_brute_force_target
rules.description: A burst of failed logins means the device is under a password attack

rules.name: R2_brute_force_source
rules.description: Whoever makes the burst of failed logins is acting as an attacker

rules.name: R3_credential_compromise
rules.description: A successful login right after brute forcing means the password was guessed

rules.name: R4_internal_attacker
rules.description: An internal machine running a password attack is itself compromised

rules.name: R5_exfiltration
rules.description: Unauthorized access followed by sustained unusual traffic to a critical asset indicates data theft

rules.name: R6_targeted_asset
rules.description: A device that receives unauthorized access attempts is being targeted

rules.name: R8_unusual_sender
rules.description: Sending unusual traffic is anomalous behaviour

rules.name: R9_unauthorized_sender
rules.description: Attempting unauthorized access is anomalous behaviour

rules.name: R10_threatens_asset
rules.description: A compromised device sending unusual traffic to a critical asset threatens it

rules.name: R11_entry_point
rules.description: The internal device that logged in to a device shortly before it was found compromised is the likely entry point

rules.name: M2_traffic_is_malicious
rules.description: Unusual traffic counts as malicious activity

rules.name: M3_bruteforce_is_malicious
rules.description: Brute forcing counts as malicious activity

rules.name: M4_access_is_malicious
rules.description: Unauthorized access counts as malicious activity

rules.name: V1_active_compromise_behaviour
rules.description: Model of attacker behaviour in this simulation: an actively compromised device produces malicious activity. Used backwards (Modus Tollens) during verification.
